newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Opposition demands authorities verify poll results.
newsitem.headline: Opposition demands authorities verify poll results.

text.p: Serbia's opposition leaders said they would demand electoral authorities confirm their victory on Tuesday after sweeping major towns in local polls.
The opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition claimed a "historic" win in the capital Belgrade and towns across the country in municipal elections over the weekend.
But the coalition expressed fears that authorities loyal to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic might try to steal votes and reverse the results.
After holding a celebratory rally in the city centre, opposition leaders led a march to city hall on Monday night to meet the head of the Belgrade electoral commission.
"We would not like the clearly expressed wish of the citizens to be forged in the end," Vuk Draskovic, head of the Serbian Renewal Movement, told the official in front of reporters.
Dragomir Lazarevic replied: "As for the verification of the electoral results -- until the moment the city electoral commission declares them publicly -- nobody has won."
He said the commission's legal obligation was to announce results by Tuesday night at the latest.

Opposition parties have representatives on electoral boards but have no access to important voting materials, making it difficult to catch any cases of fraud, Vesna Pesic, head of the Civic Alliance, told reporters.

Draskovic spoke to the crowd waiting outside the building and said the opposition would "defend" its victory, hinting at possible street demonstrations to force authorities to recognise election results.
In 1991, Draskovic led protests against state control of the media which Milosevic crushed with tanks.
The opposition leaders appeared suprised by the scale of their victory against Milosevic's leftist coalition.
In the local elections, the Zajedno (Together) coalition was comprised of the Democratic Party, the Serbian Renewal Movement and the Civic Alliance.

The municipal vote came two weeks after Milosevic's coalition scored a resounding victory in national elections -- its first big electoral test since the end of four years of war in former Yugoslavia.
But ruling Socialist party officials effectively conceded defeat in major towns in the municipal voting.
Ivica Dacic, spokesman for the Socialist Party of Serbia, said the leftist coalition won in 134 municipalities out of 174 in Serbia. But none of the big towns were on his list.
"The left (Milosevic's) coalition has 25 out of 110 councillors in the Belgrade city assembly," he said.
Loss of control of the capital's city assembly would be a blow to Milosevic and sources close to the government said Socialist leaders were "shattered" by the election results.

Political analysts said real power would remain with Milosevic, who keeps a tight grip on the police, media and finances. But the result was an unprecedented electoral embarassment for the former communist party leader.
By winning control of major municipalities, the opposition could make life difficult for Milosevic ahead of elections in the Serbian republic sometime next year, the analysts said.

In Sunday's municipal run-off -- covering 5,603 city council seats in municipalities where no candidate had managed to obtain a majority in the first round -- the opposition claimed victory in the 12 biggest Serbian towns.
Apart from Belgrade, the towns included industrial centres such as Nis, Kragujevac, Uzice, Kraljevo, Kikinda, Zrenjanin and Cacak, and Novi Sad, the provincial capital of Vojvodina.
